meta.title: MoonLit — Local-first clip recorder for Windows
meta.description: MoonLit is a local-first clip recorder for Windows x64 based on OBS Studio. Inspired by Medal.tv's idea, but open source and 100% local: no accounts, no cloud, no streaming.
hero.tagline: Local-first clip recorder for Windows x64
hero.description: Capture your game, keep a searchable local library and export trimmed clips. MoonLit takes its inspiration from Medal.tv's idea: like Office and LibreOffice, it is a similar program, but open source and 100% local — no accounts, no cloud, no streaming.
hero.releases: Downloads are published on the Releases page.
features.title: Features
features.subtitle: Everything you need to capture and keep your best moments, on your own machine.
features.detection.title: Game detection and capture
features.detection.text: Automatic target detection with Windows Graphics Capture (WGC), a privacy shield on focus loss and a safe DXGI fallback. No hooks, no injection, no virtual camera.
features.buffer.title: Replay buffer
features.buffer.text: MKV clips with four audio tracks (mixed, game, microphone and chat). Save a clip with F8 from inside the game, with a sound cue, or from the dashboard and the tray.
features.library.title: Local library
features.library.text: SQLite with FTS5 search, thumbnails and filters (All, Available, Missing). Import external files, reveal in Explorer, delete to recycle bin and reconcile on startup.
features.editor.title: Clip editor
features.editor.text: Frame-strip preview with seek, draggable trim handles, mute and gain. Keyframe-aligned MP4 export in the background with progress, cancellation and duration verification.
features.audio.title: Audio
features.audio.text: Desktop audio, microphone and chat with a compact mixer (volume and mute per source) and device selection menus. Krisp-style noise suppression (RNNoise + noise gate) on the microphone.
features.tray.title: Tray and startup
features.tray.text: Close-to-tray, minimize-to-tray and login startup with --minimize-to-tray. MoonLit branding throughout the whole app.
inspiration.title: Inspired by Medal.tv's idea
inspiration.text: Medal.tv popularized the idea of saving clips from your matches with a single touch. MoonLit takes that same idea and turns it into a similar open-source program: like Office and LibreOffice, same idea, different philosophy.
inspiration.local.title: 100% local
inspiration.local.text: Your clips live on your disk, not in a cloud.
inspiration.opensource.title: Open source
inspiration.opensource.text: Free software under GPL v2, based on OBS Studio.
inspiration.nocloud.title: No accounts
inspiration.nocloud.text: No registration, no sign-in and no telemetry.
inspiration.private.title: Private by default
inspiration.private.text: Nothing is shared unless you export it yourself.
requirements.title: Requirements
requirements.item2: A game-capable GPU for hardware encoders (NVENC, QSV or AMF); x264 is the software fallback.
install.title: Install
install.subtitle: Two options (see the latest release on GitHub Releases):
install.setup.title: Installer (MoonLit-*-Setup.exe)
install.setup.text: Per-user NSIS install, no admin needed. Installs to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\MoonLit. Uninstalling keeps your clips, database and configuration.
install.portable.title: Portable (MoonLit-*-x64.zip)
install.portable.text: Extract anywhere and run bin\64bit\MoonLit.exe. A portable_mode marker keeps configuration and data (config/ and MoonLitData/) next to the extracted ZIP.
install.signing: Signing: binaries are signed with the self-signed "MoonLit Development" certificate. On machines other than the build host, install the certificate into Trusted Root/Trusted Publisher (see docs/moonlit/MANUAL_MATRIX.md) or expect the SmartScreen "Unknown publisher" warning.
usage.title: Usage
usage.dashboard.title: Dashboard
usage.dashboard.text: A big record button starts/stops the replay buffer. "Save clip" saves the last N seconds and recent clips open the library.
usage.f8.title: F8
usage.f8.text: Saves a clip from inside the game, only when the replay buffer is active.
usage.library.title: Library
usage.library.text: Thumbnail grid with search and filters. Select a clip to open the editor (preview, trim, mute and gain) and export MP4.
usage.settings.title: Settings
usage.settings.text: Encoder (every registered OBS codec), replay length, audio tracks, recording folder, devices, chat executable, noise suppression, clip sound and login startup.
